Incorporating SLOOS signals, the FOMC’s cautiously positive tone remains appropriate but should be tempered by mixed credit conditions:
- Business credit: Most banks reported C&I standards unchanged across firm sizes, with some expecting to ease (competition), and expectations for improved C&I asset quality—mildly supportive. However, foreign banks reported weaker business loan demand and expect tighter C&I standards—offsetting.
- Commercial real estate: Banks and foreign banks expect tighter standards for CRE and construction/land development—consistent with soft business fixed investment and a headwind to capex.
- Household credit: Banks expect to tighten auto-loan standards and foresee deteriorating asset quality in auto and credit cards—drag on consumption despite better sentiment. Mortgages are a partial offset, with expected easing for GSE-eligible and nonconforming jumbo loans and improved asset quality in some categories, while subprime is little changed.
Netting these, the credit channel points to neutral-to-slightly tighter conditions outside prime mortgages, aligning with the FOMC’s “gradual” stance and balanced near-term risks but warranting a slightly less upbeat read than before.
